walkthroughs.body_html:
Angles come in four families.

Acute is less than 90°. Right is exactly 90° (a corner). Obtuse is between 90° and 180°. Reflex is bigger than 180°.

Tip: a slice of pizza is acute, the corner of a book is right, an open laptop is often obtuse.

Triangles come in flavours:

Equilateral: all 3 sides equal, all angles 60°. Isosceles: 2 equal sides, 2 equal base angles. Scalene: all sides different. Right-angled: one 90° corner.

The big rule: angles in ANY triangle add to 180°. So if two angles are 70° and 50°, the third is 180 − 70 − 50 = 60°.

A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides. To find the total of its interior angles, use:

Sum = (n − 2) × 180°

Where n = number of sides. Examples:

• Triangle (n=3): (3−2)×180 = 180°
• Quadrilateral (n=4): (4−2)×180 = 360°
• Pentagon (n=5): (5−2)×180 = 540°
• Hexagon (n=6): (6−2)×180 = 720°

options: The hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle.
c^2 represents the side opposite the largest angle that is not 90 degrees.
